name: Ichthyol (ichthammol)

lead: Ichthammol (Ichthyol, ammonium bituminosulfonate) is a thick, dark, water-soluble ointment made from sulfur-rich shale oil. Known as 'black ointment' or 'drawing salve', it is applied at 10 to 20 percent strength to inflamed skin, and people use it on spots and boils to reduce redness and help them resolve.

Dermatology reviews describe over a century of use for psoriasis, eczema, seborrheic dermatitis, leg ulcers and furuncles. It has anti-inflammatory, antibacterial and antifungal properties reported in laboratory studies, and a few small clinical studies exist.

paras: A thin layer of ointment is dabbed on the affected spot, often covered with a dressing, and left on. It is also used in compounded preparations and in glycerine packs for ear conditions.
It is described as well tolerated, but contact sensitivity to ichthammol has been reported. It has a strong smell and stains skin and fabric. Persistent or deep infections warrant clinical review.

chain: Ointment applied to the inflamed spot
Spot calms and comes to a head sooner
angle.text: People dab it on individual blemishes and boils so that redness and swelling settle. The practice rests on the traditional drawing-salve use and on the substance's anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties.

lead: Ichthammol, sold as Ichthyol, is made from sulfur-rich oil shale by distillation, sulfonation and neutralization with ammonia. It is used as a 10 or 20 percent ointment and is also called black ointment or drawing salve. German physician Paul Gerson Unna promoted its dermatological use [1].

A 2010 review in the International Journal of Dermatology describes ichthammol as employed for over a century in psoriasis, eczematous dermatitis, leg ulcers, seborrheic dermatitis and furuncles [2]. Appearance-minded users apply it to individual spots and boils to calm and draw them out.

Studies include a 2020 case series and systematic review for hidradenitis suppurativa [3], a meta-analysis in which glycerine-ichthammol gave the greatest reduction in catheter-related phlebitis among topicals tested [4], and ear trials comparing 10 percent glycerine-ichthammol with steroid-antibiotic products [5].
infobox: Available via pharmacies and for compounding

paras: Ichthammol is used for eczema, psoriasis, acne and rosacea, and dermatology guidelines cite it for acutely inflamed atopic eczema. A glycerol-ichthammol mixture is used for ear infections [1]. The 2010 review lists psoriasis, eczematous dermatitis, leg ulcers, seborrheic dermatitis and furuncles [2].

Ichthammol is reported to have anti-inflammatory, bactericidal and fungicidal properties and to act on inflammation mediators, with activity against Gram-positive bacteria [1]. A veterinary review summarizes numerous in vitro studies of these actions [6].
Bituminosulfonates are described as having very good tolerability [1], but contact sensitivity to ichthammol has been reported in case reports [7].

A 2020 case series and systematic review examined 10 percent ichthammol for hidradenitis suppurativa and its use across dermatology [3]. A 2023 meta-analysis of 12 studies (726 patients) of topical treatments for catheter-related phlebitis found glycerine-ichthammol gave the greatest reduction in phlebitis degree, noting low quantity and quality of included trials [4]. A randomized trial compared Triadcortyl with 10 percent glycerine-ichthammol for severe acute otitis externa [5].
Unna promoted ichthammol in dermatology [1], and a Texas medical journal item on lanolin and ichthyol dates to 1886 [8].
